4.5 Indeterminate Forms and L’Hôpital’s Rule

John (Johann) Bernoulli discovered a rule using derivatives to calculate limits of frac- tions whose numerators and denominators both approach zero or +q. The rule is known today as l’Hôpital’s Rule, after Guillaume de l’Hôpital. He was a French nobleman who wrote the first introductory differential calculus text, where the rule first appeared in print. Limits involving transcendental functions often require some use of the rule for their calculation.
HISTORICAL BIOGRAPHY
Guillaume François Antoine de l’Hôpital (1661–1704)
Johann Bernoulli (1667–1748)
